transcript.text:
The most common reason a dryer behaves strangely with the door is that the door isn't latching fully, or the switch that detects the closed door has failed. 1. Open the door and ensure no clothes are trapped in the seal.
2. Shut the door firmly until you hear/feel it click into place.
3. Press Start. Does the machine now start normally, or does it still indicate that the door is open (or refuse to run)? If it starts, it was likely just a latching issue. If it still won't start despite clicking shut, we'll need to look at the door switch or wiring.
it does start fine and dries ok. its after it says End, the drum keeps turning every few minutes on its own

Thanks for clarifying that. Since the machine runs and dries normally during the cycle but continues to tumble after 'End', this usually points to a mechanical drive issue rather than an electronic control fault. The most common cause is that the belt driving the drum has slipped off, stretched, or broken, so the motor keeps running (or cycling) even though the load is finished. To check this safely:
1. Unplug the dryer from the mains.
2. Open the door and try turning the drum slowly by hand.
3. Note how it feels: does it spin freely with no resistance, does it feel stiff or stuck, or do you hear a grinding noise? This will tell us if the drive mechanism is disconnected (free spinning) or obstructed (stiff).
I haven't tried turning it by hand. I'm not sure what it should feel like. It's only 3 months old, is it really the belt?

It is very unlikely to be the belt on a machine that is only 3 months old; belts rarely fail that quickly unless something has jammed them. The fact that it dries normally during the cycle suggests the drive system is working while the programme is active. The most likely cause for a new dryer tumbling randomly after 'End' is an electronic fault in the control board—specifically, a relay (a switch inside the electronics) sticking closed and sending power to the motor even when it shouldn't. This can happen due to a manufacturing defect or a glitch. To be sure this isn't a mechanical issue, please do this simple check:
1. Unplug the dryer from the mains.
2. Open the door and try turning the drum slowly by hand.
3. Tell me exactly how it feels: does it spin freely with no resistance, does it feel stiff or stuck, or do you hear a grinding noise? This will tell us if there is a physical obstruction (which would point to a belt/jam) or if the mechanics are fine (pointing back to the electronics).
I'm not really comfortable doing that, and I wouldn't know what it should feel like anyway. Is there something simpler I can check?

Since turning the drum by hand isn't comfortable for you, let's look at the simpler possibilities first. On a brand-new dryer (3 months old), mechanical failures like a broken belt are very rare. The most likely cause is actually an electronic one: a relay inside the control board may be sticking closed, keeping power to the motor even after the programme finishes. Alternatively, many modern dryers have a 'Refresh' or 'Anti-Crease' function that tumbles the clothes for 10–20 minutes after drying to prevent wrinkles. To distinguish between these:
1. When the cycle says 'End', look closely at the display. Does it mention 'Refresh', 'Anti-Crease', or similar? If so, this is likely a normal feature and not a fault.
2. Try pressing the Stop button immediately when the cycle ends. If it stops instantly, it suggests the machine thinks it's still in a post-dry phase (either a setting or an electronic glitch). Please let me know what you see on the display at 'End' and whether pressing Stop makes it halt.
The display just says End, or 0:00. Nothing about refresh or anti-crease. Opening the door stops it straight away though. I haven't tried the stop button.

The fact that opening the door stops it immediately suggests the machine is receiving power to the motor but isn't being told to stop by its electronics. Since this is only 3 months old, mechanical failure is extremely unlikely. This points strongly to a fault in the main control board (PCB). Inside the board are relays—electronic switches that turn the motor on and off. It is likely one of these relays has stuck in the 'on' position, or there is a software glitch causing it to ignore the end-of-cycle signal. Before assuming a hardware fault, let's try a full reset:
1. Unplug the dryer from the wall socket for at least 5 minutes (this drains any residual power and resets the electronics).
2. Plug it back in.
3. Start a short programme and observe what happens when it says 'End'. If it still tumbles randomly after 'End' following this reset, the control board is likely faulty. Given the appliance is under warranty (3 months old), you should contact the retailer or manufacturer for a repair or replacement rather than attempting to open the machine yourself.
